title: Kinetic Strike Tracker — Requirements Specification
author: AI agent (Claude), drafted for human review
reviewer: Bruce Dombrowski — open-question review received as issue #2 (2026-07-25); dispositions applied in v0.2.0
notes: Per SE process principle 1 (review over authoring), this document is a DRAFT. It becomes the v1.0 baseline only after human review and an approving commit.
Requirement IDs are stable per IEEE 29148. Do not renumber; deprecate instead.

Priority values: mandatory (SHALL), recommended (SHOULD), optional (MAY). Per BCP 14 (RFC 8174), keywords are normative only when written in ALL CAPS; lowercase instances of these words in rationale, notes, and prose carry no normative weight.
Verification methods: inspection, test, analysis, demonstration — per the taxonomy defined in NPR 7123.1 (and equivalently MIL-STD-961E).

open_questions contains ONLY unresolved items — the count is meant to be driven to zero. Resolved items move to resolved_questions with their resolution and the decision memorandum that records it; nothing is deleted. New questions are expected to appear as implementation proceeds; the goal is that they are answered, not that they never arise.

assumptions.text: Global seismic catalogs cannot resolve kinetic strikes at munition scale anywhere. This was measured over Iran because that is where a known strike campaign provides ground truth; the limitation is a property of the global network's detection threshold, not of that region. This was measured, not assumed: a query of the USGS FDSN event service for 2025-06-01 to 2025-07-05 over the box 31.5-36.5 N, 49.0-53.5 E — containing Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan, and spanning the entire June 2025 campaign — with NO minimum magnitude returned exactly two events, neither at any struck site. The 2025-06-22 strike on Fordow produced no catalogued USGS event whatsoever. A broader query over 25-40 N, 44-64 E returned nothing below M4.1.
assumptions.consequence: Magnitude of completeness for USGS over Iran measured approximately M4.0, and comparable figures apply across sparsely instrumented regions worldwide. Munition-scale events couple at roughly M2.0-M2.5 — two to three orders of magnitude in energy below that floor. Global-catalog sources alone are therefore insufficient, and REQ-2.4 (regional networks) is mandatory rather than recommended.

assumptions.text: Detecting events below regional catalog completeness requires independent processing of raw station waveforms — arrival-time picking across multiple stations followed by hypocentre inversion — rather than consumption of pre-computed catalog origins.
assumptions.consequence: Catalog ingestion alone bounds the system to events someone else already located. Independent triangulation (REQ-5.8, REQ-5.9) is the only path to the sub-threshold regime where most strikes occur, and is therefore the system's principal technical differentiator rather than an optional enhancement.

assumptions.text: Magnitude of completeness (Mc) for the Iranian Seismological Center catalog is spatially and temporally heterogeneous, and roughly 19% of catalog entries are reported in the literature to be non-tectonic (quarry and mine blasts).
assumptions.consequence: Anthropogenic-source contamination is expected in any regional catalog and is a discrimination problem the system must address explicitly, not an anomaly.

assumptions.text: Many regions of interest are tectonically active, Iran conspicuously so. Natural seismicity is the dominant signal in such regions and constitutes the primary false-positive source.
assumptions.consequence: Discrimination and confidence scoring are core functions, not enhancements.

assumptions.text: All data sources are open, publicly accessible, and unclassified. The system holds no classified, CUI, or otherwise controlled information.
assumptions.consequence: NIST SP 800-171 controls are not levied. Baseline hygiene and licence compliance apply.

assumptions.text: Development and initial target environment are the same machine: Apple Silicon (arm64) MacBook Pro running macOS with Xcode Command Line Tools.
assumptions.consequence: Single-platform v1. Portability is designed for but not verified on other platforms in v1.

assumptions.text: All ingested data — whether retrieved over the network or read from a local file — originates outside the trust boundary and is potentially hostile. This includes deliberately malformed structured data, adversarially crafted free text, and files supplied by a third party.
assumptions.consequence: Every parser and every output path is an attack surface. Input validation is a distinct requirement category (category 12), not an implementation detail.

assumptions.text: The project is developed openly: a public repository, open source licence, and a public development record in which planning discussions and agent interactions are published as issues.
assumptions.consequence: No credential, private datum, or unreviewed personal information may enter the repository at any point (REQ-10.6, REQ-13.3).

assumptions.text: CORRECTED 2026-07-25 (issue #23). The earlier form of this assumption was drawn from the FDSN pipe-delimited text format, which silently omits depthType, originUncertainty, and typeCertainty. The QuakeML record shows: all 13 IDC origins over the June 2025 window carry depthType 'operator assigned' with no published depth uncertainty; horizontal uncertainty ellipses range from 146x312 km to 265x1011 km; and every one is flagged typeCertainty 'suspected' with no magnitude. By contrast NEIC's Semnan origin has a 10x14 km ellipse and typeCertainty 'known', and ISN's has 6x10 km with a freely determined 22.3 km depth.
assumptions.consequence: IDC-contributed origins establish that energy was detected and roughly when, but their locations cannot support site-level attribution — an ellipse approaching 1000 km spans much of a country — and their depths are not measurements. They are a temporal signal, not a positional one. Consequently: adapters SHALL prefer formats that publish provenance (REQ-2.19), location uncertainty SHALL drive the location confidence axis (REQ-7.8), and independent triangulation (REQ-5.8/5.9) is the only route to site-level attribution.

requirements.text: The system SHALL correlate objective, publicly available geophysical observations with open-source reporting to identify and characterise candidate kinetic strike events anywhere on Earth. The data model SHALL be whole-Earth; each analysis is scoped by a configurable region of interest supplied at run time, and nothing in the data model, schema, or analysis SHALL privilege any particular region.
requirements.notes: Amended per review issue #2 (OQ-03) and issue #21. Scope is Earth. Iran and the June 2025 campaign appear only as validation cases (VC-01, VC-02, VC-04) because a documented strike campaign provides ground truth, and as the CLI's default window for reproducing those cases — not as a scope boundary.

requirements.text: The system SHALL maintain an explicit coverage model recording, for each source, the spatial extent and detection threshold (e.g. magnitude of completeness) over which that source can be expected to observe events, and SHALL treat 'no coverage' as distinct from 'no events'.
requirements.rationale: Review issue #2 (OQ-03): what we have coverage on, we have coverage on — everywhere else must be visibly unknown rather than silently empty. This requirement is the data-model half; REQ-8.8 is the presentation half.

requirements.text: The system SHALL be deterministic: for a given frozen input snapshot and a given configuration, every execution SHALL produce byte-identical analytical output.
requirements.rationale: Determinism is the project's defining characteristic and the precondition for auditability and reproducible analysis. It forbids unseeded randomness, wall-clock dependence in analysis, and unordered-container iteration on any output path.

requirements.text: The system SHALL be retrospective and analytical in nature, operating on already-published observations of events that have already occurred.
The system SHALL operate as a local, self-contained application requiring no server-side infrastructure for its v1 release.
The system SHOULD be architected so that a future browser-accessible presentation layer can be added without modification to the analysis core.
requirements.rationale: Stated intent to make this a public tool eventually. Enforced by REQ-9.2 (core/UI separation).

requirements.text: The system SHALL define a source-adapter interface such that each data source is implemented as an independent, separately testable adapter, and SHALL support adding a new source without modification to the analysis core.

The system SHALL ingest seismic events from the USGS FDSN event web service at https://earthquake.usgs.gov/fdsnws/event/1/query, using GeoJSON output and supporting the starttime, endtime, minlatitude, maxlatitude, minlongitude, maxlongitude, mindepth, maxdepth, minmagnitude, eventtype, orderby and limit parameters.
requirements.notes: Service caps results at 20000 per query and returns HTTP 400 above that; see REQ-2.8.

requirements.text: The system SHALL ingest seismic events from the EMSC SeismicPortal FDSN event web service, which provides independent regional coverage of the European-Mediterranean and Middle East region.
requirements.rationale: An independent second instrumental source is required for REQ-7.3 (independent corroboration) to be meaningful.

requirements.text: The system SHALL ingest events from the International Seismological Centre (ISC) FDSN event web service, which aggregates member-agency bulletins — including the CTBTO International Data Centre (IDC), NEIC, and regional agencies — into a single machine-readable interface.
requirements.rationale: Amended per review issue #2 (OQ-07) after a measured spike. The ISC service returned 15 events for the June 2025 window over the Fordow/Natanz/Isfahan box where USGS returned 2 — thirteen of them IDC (CTBTO) detections at depth 0.0, temporally clustered on the strike-campaign nights (evidence: requirements/evidence/isc-iran-jun2025.txt). Direct IRSC access is EXCLUDED: its data-use agreement prohibits redistribution, which is incompatible with an open tool (REQ-2.12). ISC is the compliant aggregation route. Note the reviewed ISC bulletin lags ~24 months; contributed preliminary data (IDC REB) arrives much sooner — the adapter records which it consumed per REQ-2.17.

requirements.text: The system SHALL ingest official government statements as a source class, including U.S. Central Command (USCENTCOM) public releases and press releases via its published RSS feeds.
The system SHOULD ingest curated conflict-event datasets that publish a documented coding methodology, including ACLED (Armed Conflict Location & Event Data).
requirements.notes: ACLED API access requires free registration; credentials are configuration, never committed (REQ-10.6).

requirements.text: The system MAY ingest news media and social media reporting as a corroborating source class, provided such reports are assigned the reduced confidence weighting defined in REQ-7.2 and are never used as the sole basis for a high-confidence assessment.
requirements.rationale: Explicit user direction: news sources are acceptable, but confidence is correspondingly lower.

requirements.text: Each adapter SHALL respect the documented query limits, pagination semantics, terms of service, and rate limits of its upstream source, and SHALL partition oversized time ranges into compliant sub-queries rather than issuing a request that would be rejected.

The failure, timeout, or unavailability of any single source adapter SHALL NOT terminate the ingestion run. The system SHALL record the failure, continue with remaining sources, and mark the resulting analysis as having incomplete source coverage.
The system SHALL persist the unmodified raw response of every successful source query, together with the request URL, request timestamp (UTC), HTTP status, and a SHA-256 digest of the response body.
requirements.rationale: Raw-response retention is what makes REQ-1.2 determinism testable: an analysis can be replayed against a frozen snapshot without re-querying the network.

requirements.text: The system SHALL support an offline replay mode that performs a complete analysis run against previously persisted raw responses with no network access whatsoever.
Each source adapter SHALL declare the licence or terms of use of the data it retrieves, and the system SHALL surface required attribution in its outputs.

The system SHALL support ingestion from local files as a first-class source class, accepting at minimum GeoJSON, QuakeML, CSV, and JSON, so that manually curated datasets, archived downloads, and datasets lacking a public API may be incorporated.
requirements.rationale: Several relevant sources publish bulk downloads rather than queryable APIs. File ingestion also underpins the offline replay mode of REQ-2.11 and the test fixtures of REQ-10.4.

requirements.text: File-sourced input SHALL be subject to the same validation, provenance recording, and untrusted-input handling as network-sourced input, and SHALL NOT be granted elevated trust by virtue of being local.
requirements.rationale: A file on disk carries no more assurance than an HTTP response; it may have arrived from anywhere. See category 12.

requirements.text: The system SHALL ingest space-based thermal anomaly detections from NASA FIRMS (VIIRS 375 m and MODIS active fire products) as a class A instrumental source, retaining detection time, coordinates, confidence, and fire radiative power.
requirements.rationale: FIRMS publishes discrete detections with time and position rather than raw imagery, so it normalises into the Observation model of REQ-3.1 directly. It is an instrumental observation independent of the seismic networks, and it detects strikes that produce fire but no resolvable seismic signal — directly addressing the ASM-01 detection gap. Near-real-time latency is approximately 3 hours.

requirements.text: The system MAY ingest openly licensed satellite imagery products, including Copernicus Sentinel-1 synthetic aperture radar and Sentinel-2 optical data, to support change detection and damage assessment.
requirements.notes: Deferred beyond v1. Unlike FIRMS, these are raster products requiring an imagery processing pipeline rather than event normalisation. SAR coherence change detection is the technique of interest and is unaffected by cloud or darkness.

requirements.text: The system SHALL support a curated seed dataset of known or hand-entered events, ingested from a local file, carrying the same Observation structure plus a curator attribution, and clearly marked as curated rather than instrumentally detected.
requirements.rationale: Review issue #2 (OQ-04): v1 bootstraps from hand-fed known events (e.g. the June 2025 campaign) rather than automated news scraping; automated gathering of reporting sources is decided later. Also provides ground truth for the validation cases.

requirements.text: Where a source publishes both an authoritative catalog and a preliminary or automatic feed, the system SHALL record which was used and SHALL update an observation when the authoritative revision supersedes a preliminary one, retaining the prior value.
requirements.rationale: Seismic origins are routinely revised after initial automatic publication. Silently overwriting would destroy the audit trail; ignoring revisions would retain known-superseded values.

requirements.text: Where a source offers multiple response formats, the adapter SHALL use the format that carries the most complete provenance — specifically depth determination type, origin uncertainty, and event type certainty — even at the cost of a more complex parser.
requirements.rationale: Issue #23: the FDSN text format omits depthType, originUncertainty and typeCertainty. Consuming it produced an assessment that looked confident and was not. A format that hides the quality of a measurement is not a cheaper version of one that does not; it is a different and worse input.

requirements.text: The system SHALL normalise every ingested record into a common internal Observation model, independent of source, comprising at minimum: internal identifier, source identifier, native source event identifier, source class, origin time, latitude, longitude, depth, magnitude with magnitude type, location uncertainty, reported event type, and free-text description.

All timestamps SHALL be stored, compared, and emitted in UTC using ISO 8601 representation with explicit timezone designator and millisecond precision. Local time SHALL NOT be used in storage or analysis.
All coordinates SHALL be stored as decimal degrees in WGS 84 (EPSG:4326), latitude in [-90, 90] and longitude in [-180, 180], with longitude normalised on ingest.
requirements.notes: The USGS service accepts longitude in [-360, 360]; normalisation on ingest is therefore mandatory, not incidental.

requirements.text: The system SHALL retain the native magnitude type (e.g. mb, ML, Mw, MN, md) alongside every magnitude value and SHALL NOT convert between magnitude types silently.
requirements.rationale: Magnitude estimates for the same event differ measurably between networks; silent conversion would fabricate precision.

requirements.text: Every Observation SHALL carry a stable internal identifier derived deterministically from its source identifier and native event identifier, such that re-ingesting the same record yields the same internal identifier.
requirements.rationale: A random UUID would violate REQ-1.2. The identifier must be a pure function of the record.

requirements.text: The system SHALL preserve the reported quantities exactly as published and SHALL record any derived or inferred quantity as a separate, clearly labelled field.
The system SHALL reject and log, rather than silently discard, any record failing schema or range validation.
The system SHALL persist all normalised observations, raw responses, correlations, assessments, and run metadata in a single local SQLite database file.
requirements.rationale: SQLite ships with macOS, satisfying the stdlib-first dependency posture (REQ-9.4).

requirements.text: The database SHALL carry a schema version, and the system SHALL apply forward migrations deterministically and refuse to operate against a schema version it does not recognise.

Ingestion SHALL be idempotent: re-ingesting an already-stored record SHALL update it in place rather than creating a duplicate, and SHALL leave the analytical result unchanged if the record is unchanged.
The system SHALL record, for every analysis run: run identifier, software version, git commit hash, configuration digest, source snapshot digests, and start and end timestamps in UTC.
The system SHALL NOT modify or delete previously persisted raw responses; the raw response store SHALL be append-only.

The raw response store SHALL be content-addressed: each distinct response body is stored once, keyed by its SHA-256 digest, while every retrieval SHALL still record its own request URL, timestamp, and status referencing that body. Deduplication SHALL NOT discard retrieval history.
requirements.rationale: Resolves OQ-08 (issue #22, DM-2026-006). Successive polls of an unchanged window return byte-identical bodies, so dedup is a large storage win at zero information loss. The distinction matters: the body is deduplicated, the act of retrieval is not — provenance (REQ-7.4) depends on knowing when each fetch happened, not merely what was fetched.

requirements.text: The system SHALL classify each seismic observation against the candidate source hypotheses: natural earthquake, surface or near-surface explosion, quarry or mine blast, and indeterminate.

The system SHALL apply reported focal depth as a discriminant ONLY where the source declares the depth was determined from the data. Where the source declares the depth operator-assigned, default, or otherwise not solved — or declares nothing — the system SHALL NOT apply the depth discriminant, and SHALL record that it declined and why.
requirements.rationale: Strengthened per issue #23. QuakeML depthType answers this authoritatively, replacing the earlier heuristic of guessing from the value itself. Measured: all 13 IDC origins in the June 2025 window are 'operator assigned' at depth 0.0 — under the old value-guessing heuristic a plausible reading would have classified every one as a surface explosion, over a tectonically active region (ASM-03).

requirements.text: The system SHOULD apply the mb:Ms magnitude-ratio discriminant where both body-wave and surface-wave magnitudes are published for an event.
requirements.notes: Literature indicates the spectral contribution to mb:Ms separation vanishes below approximately mb 4.5, so this discriminant is of limited value for the small events dominating this problem. Its limits SHALL be documented per REQ-5.7.

requirements.text: The system MAY apply P/S amplitude-ratio discrimination in the approximate 10-18 Hz band, which requires ingestion of waveform data rather than catalog parameters alone.
requirements.rationale: Explosions generate P waves more efficiently than S waves relative to earthquakes, and the discriminant strengthens at higher frequencies. Deferred beyond v1 because it requires an FDSN dataselect waveform pipeline and signal processing well beyond catalog ingestion.

requirements.text: The system SHALL apply a known-source exclusion, suppressing or down-weighting candidate events whose location coincides with a documented quarry, mine, or other recurring industrial blast site, and whose timing is consistent with that site's established pattern.
requirements.rationale: Directly addresses ASM-02: roughly 19% of IRSC catalog entries are reported to be blasts rather than tectonic events.

requirements.text: Every discrimination criterion SHALL be implemented as an explicit, published, human-auditable rule with stated numeric thresholds. The system SHALL NOT use opaque or statistically trained classification for source discrimination in v1.
requirements.rationale: Required by REQ-1.2 (determinism) and by the auditability premise of the project.

requirements.text: The system SHALL document, alongside each discriminant, the magnitude and distance range over which that discriminant is considered valid, and SHALL NOT apply a discriminant outside its stated range of validity.

The system SHOULD retrieve raw waveform data for stations within regional distance of the area of interest via the FDSN dataselect and station web services, together with the instrument metadata required to interpret it.
requirements.rationale: Prerequisite for REQ-5.9. Waveform access is what distinguishes this system from a catalog aggregator; per ASM-01b, catalog origins cannot reach the sub-threshold regime where strikes occur.

requirements.text: The system SHOULD determine an independent hypocentre by picking phase arrival times across three or more stations and inverting for origin time and location against a documented regional velocity model, and SHALL report the resulting location uncertainty rather than a bare point estimate.
requirements.rationale: Independent triangulation is the only mechanism by which the system can locate an event that no agency has catalogued. A location without an uncertainty estimate is not a scientific result, and for events near the detection floor the uncertainty ellipse may be large enough to change what conclusions the location supports.
requirements.notes: A minimum of three stations is required for a two-dimensional solution; four or more constrain depth. Station coverage geometry, not station count alone, governs solution quality — a poorly distributed network yields a poorly conditioned inversion regardless of how many stations contribute.

requirements.text: The system MAY apply template matching or waveform cross-correlation against known events to detect signals below the conventional single-station detection threshold.
requirements.notes: Deferred beyond v1. Relevant because repeated strikes on a single site produce near-identical waveforms at a given station, making later strikes on an already-struck target detectable at signal levels where nothing would otherwise be picked.

requirements.text: Where the system computes its own hypocentre for an event that is also catalogued by an agency, it SHALL retain both solutions and SHALL NOT silently substitute one for the other.
requirements.rationale: Divergence between an independent solution and a published one is itself an analytical signal and must remain visible.

requirements.text: The system SHALL apply a diurnal-regularity discriminant: where a spatial cell accumulates a documented minimum number of explosion-typed observations and those observations concentrate within a working-hours window while leaving a documented number of hours empty, the system SHALL reclassify them as industrial blasting and record the observed distribution as the reason. This discriminant SHALL be capable of reclassifying an event to industrial blasting but SHALL NOT be capable of promoting any event to surface explosion.
requirements.rationale: Measured (issue #25): a southern Jordan phosphate-mining cell produced 1152 explosion-typed events confined to 06:00-13:00 UTC with 14 empty hours, while Gaza produced 1425 spread across all 24 hours and peaking at night. Industry keeps working hours; war does not. This derives the industrial signature from the data rather than depending on the manually maintained registry of REQ-5.5, and it works where the depth discriminant cannot because these events carry unconstrained depths (issue #23). The one-way constraint is deliberate: a facility struck repeatedly at similar hours could mimic the pattern, so the rule may only ever move an event toward the more conservative classification.
requirements.notes: Thresholds are configuration, reported in output, and stated in DM-2026-008.

requirements.text: The system SHALL correlate observations from different sources into a single candidate Event when they fall within configurable space and time association windows.

Association windows SHALL be configurable and SHALL default to values that account for the differing spatial and temporal resolution of each source class, recognising that a news report may localise an event only to a city and a date, while a seismic origin is localised to kilometres and seconds.
The correlation algorithm SHALL be order-independent: the resulting set of candidate Events SHALL NOT depend on the order in which observations were ingested.
requirements.rationale: A greedy first-match association would make output depend on ingestion order, violating REQ-1.2.

requirements.text: The system SHALL retain every constituent observation of a candidate Event, together with the specific criterion that caused each association, and SHALL NOT collapse constituents into a summary that discards the underlying records.

The system SHALL de-duplicate the same physical event reported by multiple seismic networks under different native identifiers, and SHALL treat such de-duplicated origins as a single instrumental observation rather than as independent corroboration.
requirements.rationale: USGS and EMSC frequently publish the same origin. Counting both as independent would inflate confidence. EMSC operates an EventID service mapping identifiers across institutions, which may support this.

requirements.text: The system SHALL support candidate Events that possess no seismic observation at all, formed solely from reporting sources.
requirements.rationale: Follows directly from ASM-01: most strikes are below the seismic detection floor. Restricting Events to seismically detected ones would discard the majority of real events.

requirements.text: The system SHALL assign each candidate Event a confidence assessment computed by a published, deterministic formula, and SHALL emit the individual contributing factors alongside the resulting value.

The system SHALL assign each source to a source class carrying a distinct confidence weight, in descending order of weight: (A) instrumental geophysical observation; (B) official government statement; (C) curated conflict dataset with published methodology; (D) established news media reporting; (E) social media or unattributed user-generated content.
requirements.rationale: Direct user direction: news sources are permitted, with correspondingly lower confidence. The class structure makes that weighting explicit and auditable rather than implicit.

requirements.text: Confidence SHALL increase with the number of genuinely independent sources corroborating an Event, where sources sharing an upstream origin SHALL NOT be counted as independent.
requirements.rationale: Wire-service syndication means twenty outlets may carry one report. Counting them as twenty independent corroborations is the single most likely way for this system to produce a confident wrong answer.

requirements.text: Every assertion the system emits SHALL be traceable to the specific source records supporting it, and the system SHALL be able to reproduce that provenance chain from stored data alone.
The system SHALL distinguish and separately represent the confidence that an event occurred, the confidence in its location, and the confidence in its characterisation as a kinetic strike.
requirements.rationale: These are independent. A well-corroborated event may have poorly constrained location; a precisely located seismic event may be an ordinary earthquake.

requirements.text: The system SHALL store the individual confidence factors, not only a combined result, and SHALL isolate the presentation of confidence (numeric score, ordinal band, or both) behind an interface such that changing the representation does not invalidate stored data or require re-analysis.
requirements.rationale: Review issue #2 (OQ-05): rather than deciding numeric vs ordinal now, the design must not break when the choice is made or later changed. Storing factors and deriving the presentation makes the representation a view concern.

requirements.text: The system SHALL record disconfirming evidence, including sources that reported no event or that attributed the event to a natural cause, and SHALL reflect such evidence in the confidence assessment.

Published location uncertainty SHALL drive the location confidence axis. Where uncertainty is not published, the system SHALL report location confidence as unknown, and SHALL NOT treat an unpublished uncertainty as a small one. Where the uncertainty is too large to distinguish candidate sites, the system SHALL report the location as unusable for attribution.
requirements.rationale: Issue #23 exposed the system reporting 'moderate' location confidence for origins uncertain to +/-850 km. Silence about uncertainty is not evidence of precision.

requirements.text: The system SHALL provide a command-line interface supporting, at minimum: ingest, analyse, replay, query, and report operations.
The system SHALL export candidate Events as GeoJSON conforming to RFC 7946, with confidence and provenance carried in feature properties.
requirements.rationale: GeoJSON is directly consumable by mapping tools and by the future browser layer contemplated in REQ-1.5.

requirements.text: The system SHALL produce a human-readable report listing candidate Events with time, location, magnitude where available, contributing sources, confidence assessment, and classification.
All machine-readable output SHALL be emitted with stable key ordering and stable numeric formatting so that outputs of successive runs may be compared with a byte-level diff.
requirements.rationale: This is what makes REQ-1.2 verifiable in practice.

requirements.text: Every output SHALL carry the attribution required by the licences of the data sources contributing to it.
Every report SHALL state the detection limitations bearing on its content, and SHALL state explicitly that absence of a detected event is not evidence that no event occurred.
requirements.rationale: Follows from ASM-01. Without this, a reader may reasonably but wrongly read a sparse report as a comprehensive census.

requirements.text: Geospatial output SHALL include a coverage layer derived from the coverage model of REQ-1.6, rendering regions without adequate source coverage as visibly distinct (e.g. greyed out), so that a viewer cannot mistake unobserved regions for quiet ones.
requirements.rationale: Review issue #2 (OQ-03). The presentation half of coverage awareness: the map shows the whole Earth, and honesty about the difference between 'nothing happened' and 'we cannot see there' is rendered, not footnoted.

requirements.text: Reports SHALL clearly distinguish observed quantities from derived or inferred quantities.
The system SHALL be implemented in standard C++, compiling cleanly under the C++20 standard with Apple Clang on macOS arm64.
The system SHALL separate a presentation-independent core library from all user interface code, such that the core library contains no input or output logic beyond its defined interfaces.
requirements.rationale: This is the requirement that makes REQ-1.5 (future browser layer) achievable rather than aspirational.

requirements.text: The analysis core SHALL have no direct dependency on the network. All network access SHALL be confined to source adapters, and the core SHALL be exercisable entirely from stored data.

The system SHALL rely on the C++ standard library and operating-system-provided libraries to the greatest extent practicable. Third-party runtime dependencies SHALL be avoided, and any proposed third-party dependency SHALL require a recorded decision memorandum justifying it.
requirements.rationale: Direct user direction. macOS provides libcurl, libsqlite3, and libz, so HTTPS retrieval and persistence are achievable with no third-party code. JSON parsing has no standard-library facility and is therefore expected to be implemented in-project.

requirements.text: Platform-specific code SHALL be isolated behind interfaces so that porting to another platform does not require modification of the analysis core.

The build SHALL succeed from a clean checkout on a macOS machine with Xcode Command Line Tools and CMake installed. Build-time tooling beyond these two SHALL NOT be required, and no third-party runtime dependency is introduced by the build system.
requirements.rationale: Amended per review issue #2 (OQ-01): CMake approved as a build-time tool (DM-2026-001). The stdlib-first posture of REQ-9.4 governs runtime dependencies and is unaffected.

requirements.text: The system SHALL treat compiler warnings as errors under a documented warning set, and SHALL NOT suppress a warning without a recorded justification.
The system SHALL complete a full analysis run over one year of catalog data for the region of interest, from stored data, in under 60 seconds on the target machine.
requirements.notes: Threshold is provisional pending measurement of real data volume; to be confirmed at baseline review.

requirements.text: The system SHALL provide an automated test suite executable by a single command, covering at minimum: normalisation, correlation order-independence, discrimination thresholds, confidence computation, and end-to-end determinism.
The test suite SHALL include a determinism test that executes a complete analysis twice against a fixed stored snapshot and asserts byte-identical output.
Test fixtures SHALL include captured real responses from each supported source, committed to the repository, so that the suite runs without network access.
All network retrieval SHALL use TLS with certificate verification enabled. Certificate verification SHALL NOT be disabled.
requirements.notes: TLS 1.2 minimum, TLS 1.3 preferred, per RFC 8446. The client cannot mandate 1.3-only: upstream seismic services control their own endpoints.

requirements.text: API keys and credentials SHALL be supplied by configuration or environment and SHALL NOT be committed to version control, appear in logs, or appear in outputs.
requirements.notes: The repository is public. This requirement is load-bearing.

requirements.text: The project SHALL maintain a CHANGELOG.md per Keep a Changelog and SHALL version releases per Semantic Versioning.
The system SHALL log its operations to a persistent log with UTC timestamps and severity levels sufficient to reconstruct a run after the fact.
The system SHALL ingest only data that is publicly available and lawfully accessible. It SHALL NOT ingest classified, controlled unclassified, or access-restricted information.

The system SHALL NOT provide targeting, aim-point, engagement, or other operational fire-support functionality. It is an after-the-fact analytical tool operating on published reports of events that have already occurred.
requirements.rationale: Recorded as an explicit scope boundary so that the exclusion is auditable and cannot drift silently through feature accretion.

requirements.text: The system SHALL NOT identify, track, or profile private individuals. Its unit of analysis is the event, not the person.

The system SHALL NOT present its assessments as authoritative or verified determinations of fact, and SHALL characterise its outputs as candidate assessments derived from open sources with stated confidence.

Casualty estimation, damage assessment, and attribution of responsibility to a specific actor are outside the scope of v1. Where a source itself reports such information, the system SHALL carry it as a source-attributed quotation and SHALL NOT derive its own conclusion.

categories.name: Input Validation and Untrusted Data Handling

requirements.text: The system SHALL treat all ingested data, from every source and every transport including local files, as untrusted input, and SHALL validate it against an explicit schema before it is admitted to the data model.
All database access SHALL use parameterised statements. String concatenation SHALL NOT be used to construct any SQL statement incorporating source-derived data.
All parsers SHALL enforce documented bounds on input size, nesting depth, string length, array length, and numeric range, and SHALL fail safely on violation rather than exhausting memory or stack.
requirements.rationale: A hand-written recursive-descent JSON parser, which REQ-9.4 makes likely, is trivially driven to stack exhaustion by deeply nested input unless depth is explicitly bounded. This is the most probable memory-safety defect in the system as specified.

requirements.text: The system SHALL NOT execute, evaluate, deserialise into executable form, or pass to a shell any content derived from a source.

File paths derived from configuration or source content SHALL be canonicalised and confirmed to resolve within an expected base directory, rejecting traversal sequences and symbolic links escaping that directory.

Source-derived text SHALL be neutralised for the specific output context in which it is rendered, including escaping of spreadsheet formula-initiating characters in CSV output, escaping of markup in any HTML output, and control-character stripping in terminal and log output.
requirements.rationale: Free-text fields carry adversary-controlled content. CSV formula injection and terminal escape-sequence injection are both realised through fields that appear inert. The future browser layer of REQ-1.5 makes the markup case load-bearing.

requirements.text: Source-derived free text SHALL be stored and processed strictly as data. Should any future component submit such text to a language model or other instruction-following system, that text SHALL be delimited and identified as untrusted content, and any instruction it contains SHALL NOT be acted upon.
requirements.rationale: Ingesting adversary-authored news and social media text creates a prompt-injection path the moment that text reaches an instruction-following consumer. Recording the constraint now, while no such component exists, is cheaper than retrofitting it after one is added.

requirements.text: The system SHALL validate TLS certificates on every retrieval, SHALL NOT follow redirects to non-TLS schemes, and SHALL bound response size, redirect count, and request timeout.

The test suite SHALL include malformed, adversarial, and boundary-case inputs for every parser, including truncated input, invalid encoding, deeply nested structures, oversized fields, and injection payloads for each output context.
The system SHALL record the integrity digest of every ingested file alongside its provenance, so that a later change to a file used in a prior analysis is detectable.
The project SHALL be released under an OSI-approved open source licence, identified by SPDX identifier in a LICENSE file at the repository root and referenced from the README.
requirements.notes: Satisfied: Apache-2.0 selected per DM-2026-002 (resolves OQ-02). LICENSE at repository root, SPDX identifier Apache-2.0.

requirements.text: Planning and design sessions SHALL be archived to the public repository issue tracker as a transcript record, labelled to distinguish human direction from agent output, in accordance with Phase 5 of the governing systems engineering process.
requirements.rationale: The development record is itself a project artifact under the open development posture of ASM-07. Session transcripts are retained locally by the agent harness and are published on explicit human direction.

requirements.text: Any transcript, log, or record published to the public repository SHALL be reviewed for credentials, personal information, and private third-party data before publication.
requirements.rationale: Automatic publication of a raw session transcript to a public repository would otherwise be an uncontrolled disclosure path. Review is a precondition of publication, not a follow-up to it.

requirements.text: Every design decision having more than one reasonable option SHALL be recorded as a decision memorandum under docs/decisions, numbered DM-YYYY-NNN, stating the options considered and the rationale for the selection.
Each requirement in this document SHALL be traceable forward to its implementing source location and its verifying test, recorded in a verification matrix under docs/verification.
Each release SHOULD include a software bill of materials enumerating the toolchain, OS-provided libraries linked, and any third-party components, in SPDX or CycloneDX format.
requirements.rationale: External standards review (issue #20). Under the stdlib-first posture the SBOM is small — which is exactly why it is cheap to produce and worth having for supply-chain auditability.

resolved_questions.question: Build system: hand-written Makefile (zero install, satisfies REQ-9.6 today) versus CMake (conventional for C++, better path to a future WASM or cross-platform build, but requires installing cmake, which is not currently present on the target machine).
resolved_questions.resolution: (review issue #2): CMake approved for install on the target environment. Recorded in DM-2026-001; REQ-9.6 amended.

resolved_questions.question: Which OSI-approved licence. Open source is decided (REQ-13.1); the specific licence is not. Apache-2.0 provides an express patent grant and a contributor patent-retaliation clause, which suits a publicly developed tool in a defence-adjacent domain; MIT is shorter and more permissive but grants no patent rights.
resolved_questions.resolution: Apache-2.0, by human directive. Recorded in DM-2026-002; LICENSE file added.

resolved_questions.question: Whether independent triangulation (REQ-5.8, REQ-5.9) is in scope for v1 or deferred. It is the capability that reaches below catalog threshold per ASM-01b, and is therefore the difference between a catalog aggregator and a detection system — but it is also, by a wide margin, the largest single body of work in this specification.
resolved_questions.resolution: (review issue #2): independent triangulation deferred from v1; tracked on the backlog (GitHub issue). REQ-5.8/5.9 remain recommended for a future release.

resolved_questions.question: Whether IRSC exposes a machine-readable interface, or whether regional catalog access requires HTML scraping or a federated FDSN data centre intermediary. REQ-2.4 is mandatory but its implementation route is unverified.
resolved_questions.resolution: (review issue #2, agent research spike): ISC FDSN event service is the aggregation route — returns IDC (CTBTO), NEIC, and regional-agency origins for the region; 13 depth-0.0 IDC detections on June 2025 strike nights confirm reachability of strike-scale events. Direct IRSC access excluded: data-use agreement prohibits redistribution. REQ-2.4 amended; evidence committed.

resolved_questions.question: Precise region-of-interest bounding box, and whether it is fixed or user-configurable per run.
resolved_questions.resolution: (review issue #2): whole-Earth data model with configurable ROI; explicit coverage model with greyed-out no-coverage regions. REQ-1.1 amended; REQ-1.6 and REQ-8.8 added.

resolved_questions.question: Whether v1 includes any news or social ingestion at all, or defers all of source class D and E to v2. REQ-2.7 currently makes it optional.
resolved_questions.resolution: (review issue #2): v1 bootstraps from a hand-curated seed dataset of known events (REQ-2.18); automated news/social gathering decided later. REQ-2.7 remains optional.

resolved_questions.question: Whether the confidence assessment is emitted as a numeric score or as ordinal bands. Ordinal bands resist false precision; numeric scores sort and threshold more naturally.
resolved_questions.resolution: (review issue #2): design for representation change — store factors, derive presentation (REQ-7.7). Numeric-vs-ordinal choice deferred without risk.

resolved_questions.question: Raw-response retention policy. REQ-4.5 makes the raw store append-only and REQ-2.10 requires persisting every response, so with whole-Earth scope (REQ-1.1) and repeated ingestion the database grows without bound — a single year of daily multi-source polling is plausibly tens of GB. Three options: (a) truly unbounded, simplest and most faithful to REQ-4.5, disk grows forever; (b) age-based export of old raw bodies to external files, keeping digests and metadata in the database so provenance chains still resolve (REQ-7.4) while the working DB stays lean; (c) content-addressed dedup, storing each distinct body once keyed by SHA-256 — successive polls of an unchanged window return byte-identical bodies, so this is likely a large win with zero information loss, and it composes with either (a) or (b).
resolved_questions.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-07-25 (issue #22): option (c) content-addressed dedup adopted unconditionally per DM-2026-006. Raw bodies stored once keyed by SHA-256; retrieval metadata still recorded per request. Archival (option b) deferred until real ingestion volume is measured.

resolved_questions.question: Whether to adopt a diurnal-pattern discriminant that identifies industrial blasting from its working-hours signature rather than from a registry of known sites.
resolved_questions.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-07-25 (issue #25): adopted per recommendation. Supporting discriminant only — it may reclassify to industrial-blast but never promote to surface-explosion. Grid 0.1 degrees, minimum 30 events per cell, triggers when >=90% of a cell's events fall within a 10-hour window AND at least 6 hours are empty. Recorded in DM-2026-008; implemented as REQ-5.12.

deferred_to_future_release: Independent triangulation from raw waveforms (REQ-5.8, REQ-5.9) — deferred per review issue #2 (OQ-06), tracked on the backlog
Satellite imagery products and SAR change detection (REQ-2.16)
Real-time streaming ingestion via the EMSC WebSocket feed

validation_cases.name: June 2025 strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities
validation_cases.description: Strikes on Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan during 13-25 June 2025. USGS catalogued no event at any struck site at any magnitude, while regional reporting indicates seismic signals near M2.5 at Fordow.
validation_cases.tests: REQ-2.4 (regional networks are necessary), REQ-8.6 (absence of detection is not absence of event), ASM-01.
validation_cases.expected_behaviour: The system detects nothing from USGS alone, and reports that source coverage was insufficient rather than reporting that no strike occurred.

validation_cases.name: Semnan M4.9, 2025-06-20 17:49:14 UTC, 35.396 N 53.025 E
validation_cases.description: A natural earthquake of mww 4.9 west of Semnan, near Iranian missile and aerospace infrastructure, which prompted contemporaneous press speculation of an underground nuclear test.
validation_cases.tests: REQ-5.1 (classification), REQ-7.2 (source class weighting), REQ-7.6 (disconfirming evidence), REQ-11.4 (no authoritative claims).
validation_cases.expected_behaviour: Class A instrumental evidence classifies the event as a natural earthquake and outweighs class D speculation. The system records the conflict between source classes rather than resolving it silently in favour of either.

validation_cases.name: Fixed-depth artefact
validation_cases.description: Every USGS origin returned for the region in the June 2025 window carries a depth of exactly 10.0 km, the agency's default for poorly constrained depths.
validation_cases.tests: REQ-5.2 (depth discriminant must not treat fixed depths as measurements).
validation_cases.expected_behaviour: The system recognises the fixed default and declines to apply the depth discriminant, rather than reading 10 km as evidence of a deep source or 0 km as evidence of a surface source.

validation_cases.name: IDC detections, June 2025 — usable in time, unusable in position
validation_cases.description: Thirteen IDC (CTBTO) origins over central/western Iran, 2025-06-13 to 2025-06-22, clustered on strike nights. QuakeML shows all carry depthType 'operator assigned', typeCertainty 'suspected', no magnitude, and horizontal uncertainty ellipses of 146x312 km to 265x1011 km. Same window contains NEIC's Semnan origin (10x14 km, 'known') and an ISN origin (6x10 km, freely determined 22.3 km depth).
validation_cases.tests: REQ-2.19 (provenance-carrying formats), REQ-5.2 (depthType governs the depth discriminant), REQ-7.8 (uncertainty drives location confidence), REQ-8.7 (observed vs derived).
validation_cases.expected_behaviour: The system reports location confidence 'unusable' for the IDC origins, declines the depth discriminant because depthType says the depth was assigned rather than solved, and surfaces the source's own 'suspected' hedge. It does NOT attribute any of them to a named facility.

validation_cases.name: Minab school strike, 2026-02-28 — documented incident, zero instrumental detection
validation_cases.description: A girls' primary school in Minab, Hormozgan province, Iran, reported struck on 2026-02-28 with ~165-175 killed, condemned by UN human rights experts and UNESCO. Encoded as a curated observation (REQ-2.18) and compared against the instrumental record: 54 observations across five months over the whole Hormuz region, EVERY one typed 'earthquake', none typed 'explosion'. On the date itself the region produced one catalogued event, ~215 km distant, typed earthquake, with +/-82 km uncertainty.
validation_cases.tests: REQ-8.6 (absence of detection is not absence of event), REQ-2.18 (curated seed), REQ-6.1/6.2 (association windows), REQ-7.5 (occurrence vs characterisation), REQ-11.4/11.5 (no verified claims, no derived casualties), REQ-1.6 (coverage model).
validation_cases.expected_behaviour: The curated event is reported standing alone — 'independent sources: 1 (instrumental 0)' — and is NOT associated with the distant IDC event. The report states that no instrumental corroboration was available and does not imply the incident did not occur. This is the reference case for the honest-reporting requirement.
